title: Google Renames Gemini Features: Gems Become Skills, Spark Becomes Task
excerpt: Personal Gems migrate automatically to Skills from November 17, 2026, Spark moves into the main chat as Task, and Scheduled Actions stay separate. Here is what each one does.
body:
• Google begins automatically migrating Gemini Gems to a new format called Skills on November 17, 2026 for personal accounts; Workspace business and non-profit accounts follow in March 2027 and education accounts in June 2027.
  • Skills live in the main chat: type "/" to apply one, stack several in one conversation, or let Gemini apply one itself. Gems each ran in a separate window.
  • Spark, Google's background agent, folds into the main chat as "Task," with a Chat and Task switch above the prompt box. Scheduled Actions — timed prompts, up to 10 at once — stay separate.
  • Before November 17: back up each Gem's instructions and download its knowledge files, because built-in Gem tools including Canvas, Deep Research and Guided Learning do not work with Skills yet.

Google is renaming two of Gemini's main features at once, with changes reaching personal accounts on November 17, 2026. Gems become Skills, and Spark, the background agent launched at I/O in May 2026, moves into the main chat as Task. A third feature, Scheduled Actions, keeps its name. Android Police's field guide, published October 18, sets out what each feature does after the reshuffle.

Gems Become Skills, Inside the Main Chat

Gems, launched in 2024, are custom versions of Gemini with their own instructions and knowledge files. Each Gem runs as a standalone bot in its own window. Skills keep the custom instructions but move them into the main Gemini chat: users type "/" in the prompt box and pick a Skill, and Gemini can also apply one on its own when it judges one relevant.

The practical upgrade is stacking. Multiple Skills can run in a single conversation — one enforcing brand guidelines, another setting writing tone — where a Gem session allowed only one configuration at a time. Example Skills include preparing for presentations, matching a writing style and getting different perspectives, according to 9to5Google.

The migration is automatic, and Skills will be available for all free users who do not have Spark; they began rolling out globally on September 30. Gaps remain: most built-in Gem tools, including Canvas, Deep Research, Guided Learning and media generation, do not work with Skills yet, Android Police reported. Sharing Skills by link and attaching Drive files are coming in the following weeks, Google told 9to5Google.

Spark Becomes Task

Spark is Google's always-on background agent. It runs on Google Cloud virtual machines, so it keeps working after a user closes a laptop or locks a phone, and it can start when an event happens rather than at a set time. It is designed to ask for approval before sending a message, changing data, making a purchase or submitting a web form, and to hand control back when a site asks for a password or payment details. Users can run up to 15 tasks at once; it requires a Google AI Pro or Ultra subscription with Keep Activity on.

In the redesign, Spark appears as "Task" in a Chat and Task switch next to the prompt box, and its settings page is now called Task settings, Android Police reported. 9to5Google's report adds that "Spark" disappears from the navigation drawer, chats and Spark tasks merge into one history filtered by All, Ready, Needs attention and In progress, and a new Scheduled page groups items as Active, Paused, Completed and Suggested. The change is rolling out as a server-side update on Android; 9to5Google was not seeing it on iOS or the web.

"new home for Spark: Start new tasks anytime and keep track of them in your chats" — Google, as quoted by 9to5Google

Scheduled Actions Are the Third Piece

Scheduled Actions, available since 2025, are the simplest of the three: a user writes a prompt, sets when and how often it runs, and Gemini prepares the result in the background. Users can have up to 10 running at once, results arrive as an unread chat on the web or a push notification on mobile, and the feature no longer needs a subscription, though it is still rolling out to free accounts and requires Keep Activity on.

Its limits explain why Spark exists alongside it. Gemini prepares each result in the hour before delivery, so it suits content that does not change by the minute — Google's examples are a morning digest of calendar, to-do list and emails, and a daily forecast with outfit ideas. Location is fixed at setup. A Spark task can instead react to events, such as a fare drop, and run multistep jobs across apps while the user is away.

What Users Should Do Before November 17

Three checks cover most users. Back up Gems — copy each Gem's instructions and download its knowledge files. Test any Gem that depends on Canvas, Deep Research, Guided Learning or media generation, because those tools do not yet work inside Skills. And pick by need: Skills for repeatable instructions, a Scheduled Action for a timed briefing without a subscription, and Task only for work that must react to events across apps while you are away.
